record.file_problem: GitHub repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README says the repository reproduces the published refusal-direction technique and reports ablation results on new models. It measures refusals after direction-based weight edits, along with capability outcomes.
record.gate_note: The direction-scan values are used to choose directions and layers, so they are not recorded as result rows. The README reports no addition/steering experiment. The listed result files are not independently inspected; only outcomes stated in the README are recorded.
record.test_reason: The repository applies the original difference-in-means direction and weight-orthogonalization recipe to a new 35B MoE model. It reports harmful-request refusals, matched benign false refusals and coding capability for several edit variants and for a community abliterated upload.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The README concludes that per-layer ablation on all layers without the embedding edit removes refusals at no measurable coding or speed cost on this MoE model. It finds that the original recipe's embedding edit, late-layer-only editing and a single global direction each fail, and that the community upload was a no-op. It adds that a same-recipe Qwen pair shows no capability loss, and leaves the HF-port loss and the DeepSeek derailments as open items.
record.recipe_differences: The repo says it follows and reproduces the published technique, measuring harmful-minus-benign mean directions and editing weights. Its successful configuration uses separate per-layer directions and omits the embedding edit; it also tests MoE-specific weight layouts and community uploads. The repository is a measurement study/tool with scripts and results, not a replication package distributing weights.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with the direction configuration (one global versus per-layer), whether the token embedding is edited, the edited layer range, the scale for embedding-inclusive edits, and the checkpoint/format and serving path (MLX versus HF safetensors/vLLM).
record.problems: The refusal judge is a deliberately simple marker list, though the README says answers were read for every matrix row. Refusal evaluation uses 12 harmful and 12 matched benign prompts. No uncertainty estimates are stated. The HF-port capability loss is not root-caused, and the DeepSeek-V4-Flash comparison does not isolate ablation from speculative decoding.
record.rows_left_out: No results are omitted under the 60-row limit. Direction-scan separations are left out because the README presents them as inputs for choosing the best layer/directions, not as outcome results.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts was not tested. A truly single shared direction worked only partially (r6); success needed per-layer directions.
Only one community upload of Ornith was checked for refusal. The Qwen pair has no refusal result, so released models are not covered generally.
Affine, cone or multi-direction structure within a layer was not tested. The study compares only one global direction against per-layer directions.
There is no comparison against non-reasoning models and no analysis of the reasoning trace beyond the judging note.

missing.what: A community-abliterated DeepSeek-V4-Flash derailed in 3 of 12 agentic tasks against 0 for the non-ablated comparison. Speculative decoding was not isolated from the ablation.
Earlier abliterated Qwen scores of 30 to 67 percent, which the authors attribute to bad conversions and a broken CUDA path rather than the ablation.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is a README only, from 12 harmful and 12 benign probes, with a marker-list judge the authors say they checked by hand. No uncertainty is reported. V4 was dropped: per-layer versus global directions bears on V1's single-direction wording, not on multi-direction structure. The V8 link rests on the README's statement that these models deliberate before answering.

versions.untested_parts: Adding the direction to induce refusals on harmless requests was not tested. The successful ablation used per-layer directions, not one shared direction.
The README reports community-upload and own-build outcomes only for the named models; it does not establish results for released models generally.
No attack suppression or training against ablation is reported.
Affine or cone descriptions are not tested; the comparison is between one global direction and per-layer directions.
No separate harmfulness judgment measure is reported.
No language or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal training methods or training stages is reported.
